items.title: Noam Brown — Agent swarms and alignment
items.hook: A high-value deep dive on multi-agent coordination: context forking, agent-to-agent messaging and parallel cognitive work—plus why longer agent horizons make evaluation harder.

items.title: Vercel data-science agent: simpler tools doubled eval scores
items.hook: A strong counterpoint to ever-growing agent harnesses: Vercel reportedly improved its data-science agent by stripping specialized tools back to bash plus file read/write. A perfect eval question for your own skills.

items.title: GPT-4 predictable scaling: capability from more compute
items.hook: The useful old idea behind today's scaling debates: capability gains could be forecast from smaller training runs before the expensive final run.

items.title: Andrew Ng: skills for using coding agents effectively
items.hook: A compact framework for what humans still need to get good at when coding agents become more autonomous: planning, context, verification and knowing when to intervene.

items.title: How to Prompt Claude 5: 7 Essential Rules from Anthropic
items.hook: Less step-by-step micromanagement, more delegation: give the whole job, context, guardrails and a crisp definition of done.

items.title: Don't Ship Skills Without Evals — Philipp Schmid
items.hook: Almost exactly the experiment you need for reusable agent skills: ablate the skill, isolate runs, measure it, and delete it when the base model catches up.

items.title: How We Built an Agent-First CLI — Vercel
items.hook: Design CLIs as predictable machine contracts: stable output, structured JSON, explicit errors and discoverable help instead of hoping agents can scrape human interfaces.

items.title: The paradox at the heart of AI and science | Terence Tao
items.hook: AI can get you to the answer faster while quietly stealing the wrong turns that build understanding. Tao's helicopter-vs-hike metaphor is worth sitting with.

items.title: How Will The Universe Die?
items.hook: A tiny science break on the competing ways cosmologists think the universe might end.

items.title: The FIRST Ferrari Electric Car
items.hook: Ferrari's first EV is a quick design-and-technology curiosity: what changes when an identity built around combustion goes electric?

items.title: Stanford CS153 Frontier Systems | Scale, AGI, and the Future of Everything
items.hook: The most relevant part isn't AGI speculation: it's which thinking, writing, coding and verification muscles we should deliberately keep exercising when AI can do the task.

items.title: Why The Harness Matters More Than The Model | YC Paper Club
items.hook: The deep version of a theme you've been circling: reliable agents emerge from state, context, tools, memory and control loops—not just a smarter model.

items.title: MCP Just Got a Whole Lot Better — Neon
items.hook: A useful MCP design shift: stop preloading giant tool catalogs; make tools progressively discoverable and expose higher-level workflows.

items.title: Claude Code internals: CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks and subagents — Lydia Hallie
items.hook: A guided mental model of Claude Code internals, especially useful for your skills-vs-hooks and subagent-orchestration questions.

items.title: Robots Just Had Their GPT-3 Moment
items.hook: The interesting robotics claim isn't one-shot magic: huge pretraining may let a robot use a video demonstration as an in-context task prompt.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra: 20 Hours of Admin — Nate B Jones
items.hook: A concrete manager-agent pattern: gather constraints and approval points once, then let parallel executors handle research, forms, dependencies and retries.

items.title: Satya Nadella on the AI Doomer Slowdown, Microsoft's Master Plan & Who Wins AI
items.hook: Microsoft's platform view of AI diffusion, interoperability, third-party safety testing and agent risks such as reward hacking.

items.title: Elon Musk & Gwynne Shotwell on AI Risks, Starship and Terafab
items.hook: A broader industrial/space conversation, with one particularly interesting idea: rival AI labs adversarially testing each other's models before release.

items.title: JD Vance on AI, Entitlement Fraud, Iran War, Israel, H-1B Abuse & the Midterms
items.hook: Current US policy context spanning AI/data-center power, immigration, deficits and foreign policy. Treat the political/economic assertions as Vance's positions rather than settled facts.

items.title: Jenkins Won DevOps, Yet Nobody Uses It Willingly
items.hook: A platform-engineering look at why flexible tools become nearly impossible to replace once years of plugins, jobs and custom behavior accumulate around them.

items.title: Star Trek: The Original Series - Season One - re:View
items.hook: Not everything here needs to improve your career. A long-form Star Trek season-one discussion for when entertainment is exactly what you want.

items.title: Azure agents framework
items.hook: A real course rather than a snack. Keep it for a deliberate learning block: Agent Framework, MCP, workflows, multi-agent orchestration and A2A are the high-value sections.
